title: Schema assertion + auto-repair harness for low-precision model outputs (FP8/INT8)
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: During recent FP8/INT8 calibration runs we observed a class of failures where outputs nominally conforming in float32 drift into minor schema violations (wrong types, missing keys, truncated arrays) that break downstream ingestion. Current JSON schema tests flag regressions but leave engineering triage to manually inspect many low-signal diffs.

Problem: Manual triage scales poorly. Some failures are harmless (e.g., numeric vs string for ID fields), others require model/regimen changes. We lack a reproducible harness that (1) exercises multiple quant profiles across representative prompts, (2) classifies violation types, (3) attempts safe auto-repair heuristics, and (4) surfaces deterministic metrics tied to calibration parameters so calibration workflows can optimize for structured-output fidelity.

Proposal: Build a test harness + pipeline that runs a matrix of model variants (float32, FP8 config A/B, INT8 static/dynamic) against a curated prompt set targeting function-calling / structured output patterns. For each response the harness will: (a) run strict JSON Schema assertion, (b) produce a compact canonical diff of violations, (c) run a prioritized set of auto-repair heuristics (type coercion, default injection, array flattening, enum normalization) with conservative rules and provenance, (d) re-validate post-repair and mark whether repair succeeded or would mask a potential correctness bug, and (e) aggregate per-field and per-prompt metrics (violation rate, repair success, repair class distribution, token delta).

Key design decisions / constraints: Heuristics must be auditable and reversible — repairs attach metadata explaining the rule, confidence and original value. Repairs are only applied in the harness for triage; they are not used in production responses unless explicitly approved by model owners. The harness should be extensible (plugin-based repair rules) and run in CI for PRs touching calibration or quant profiles.

Why unique: Existing fuzz and calibration suites exercise quantization fidelity at loss/likelihood and token-level metrics but do not produce actionable, categorized schema-failure signals or safe repair suggestions. This harness bridges calibration, eval, and triage workflows to reduce mean time to resolution for structured-output regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs matrix of at least 4 quant variants (float32, FP8-A, FP8-B, INT8) against curated 2k prompt suite with reproducible seeds
JSON Schema assertion pipeline produces per-field violation counts and top-5 diff examples per violation class
Auto-repair module implements 6 conservative heuristics (type coercion, numeric parse, default injection, missing-key add, enum normalization, array unwrapping) and records provenance for each repair
Post-repair validation status and a human-review flag are exported to a dashboard for triage
CI gate that fails if repairable violation rate > 5% for release-target quant profiles (configurable per-release)
Documentation (Confluence) and a public-runbook describing when to accept repairs vs escalate to model/regimen changes
tasks: Design harness API + config schema (input: model variant matrix, prompts, schema) — draft spec and examples
Implement strict JSON Schema assertion worker with deterministic canonicalization (stable key order, whitespace-insensitive)
Prototype 6 auto-repair heuristics with unit tests and provenance metadata
Integrate harness runner with existing calibration pipeline so quant runs can be replayed end-to-end
Create dashboard view showing per-field violation heatmap and repair outcomes (Grafana/Observable)
Add CI job to run the harness on PRs touching quantization/config paths
Write runbook + Confluence design doc and link to sample archetype diffs
Collect initial 2k prompt suite and label failure-priority buckets (business-critical vs tolerant)
comments: 2026-02-24 Arjun Patel: Spiked a prototype that canonicalizes outputs and runs ajv-based schema checks. Observed ~1.8% repairable violations on FP8-A with local seed set. Uploaded raw diffs to S3 (link below).

2026-03-02 Maya Chen: PMs want a clear signal for customer-impacting regressions. Added customer_impact bucketting to acceptance criteria and will prioritize fields used by API contracts (id/timestamp/action).

2026-03-07 Engineering review: Decided repairs must be conservative. Rejected aggressive inference heuristics (e.g., guessing missing nested objects) unless accompanied by high-confidence model signals. Added provenance requirement.

2026-03-10 Design feedback (R. Torres): Make repair UX explicit in Console — present suggested fixes with 'apply' button for model owner to accept when promoting quantized rollout. Will collaborate on Dashboard mockups.
2026-03-12 QA note: Unit tests for numeric parse and enum normalization cover edge cases. Found a flaky case when arrays are truncated mid-token; added a deterministic padding rule to tasks list.
